symbols.name: source chunk
symbols.meaning: The address chunk that the addition reads, whose selected bits are XORed into the target.
symbols.quote: Packed selected-bit addition acts on two disjoint [address fields](address-field.md) of equal width, the source $\mathcal{X}$ and the target $\mathcal{W}$.

symbols.name: target chunk
symbols.meaning: The address chunk that the addition changes, whose selected bits receive the XOR.
symbols.quote: Packed selected-bit addition acts on two disjoint [address fields](address-field.md) of equal width, the source $\mathcal{X}$ and the target $\mathcal{W}$.

symbols.name: scratch chunk
symbols.meaning: The third address chunk, whose arbitrary initial value is restored at the end.
symbols.quote: Packed selected-bit addition uses its third chunk as [scratch storage](scratch-storage.md), $\mathcal{T}$, whose initial value is arbitrary and must be restored.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of address bits in each chunk, equal to the number of segments times the segment width.
symbols.quote: Each chunk has width $\lambda$ bits, cut into $\nu$ segments of $\mu$ bits, so $\lambda = \nu\mu$.

symbols.name: segments per chunk
symbols.meaning: The number of segments into which each chunk is cut.
symbols.quote: Each chunk has width $\lambda$ bits, cut into $\nu$ segments of $\mu$ bits, so $\lambda = \nu\mu$.

symbols.name: segment width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each segment of a chunk.
symbols.quote: Each chunk has width $\lambda$ bits, cut into $\nu$ segments of $\mu$ bits, so $\lambda = \nu\mu$.

symbols.name: segment index
symbols.meaning: The index of a segment within a chunk, running from 0 to nu minus 1.
symbols.quote: The selected bit of segment $\sigma$ is its lowest bit, at position $\rho+\sigma\mu$ for $0\le\sigma<\nu$, where $\sigma$ is a segment index.

symbols.name: guard value
symbols.meaning: The integer formed by the non-selected bits of a segment, which lies between 0 and 2 to the power of mu minus 1, minus 1.
symbols.quote: The other $\mu-1$ bits of a segment form its guard, whose value $\gamma$ lies between $0$ and $2^{\mu-1}-1$.

symbols.name: control bit
symbols.meaning: The bit that decides whether a controlled update is applied.
symbols.quote: For a control bit $\beta\in\{0,1\}$, a cyclic shift of $\mathcal{W}$ by $\pm 2^{\rho+\sigma\mu}$ adds $\pm 1$ to the value of segment $\sigma$, with sign $-1$ when the selected bit is $1$ and $+1$ when it is $0$.

symbols.name: target segment value
symbols.meaning: The value of a segment of the target chunk during the eight updates.
symbols.quote: For a segment of $\mathcal{W}$ with value $\xi$ and the corresponding segment of $\mathcal{T}$ with value $\eta$, the construction uses eight controlled updates.

symbols.name: scratch segment value
symbols.meaning: The value of the corresponding segment of the scratch chunk during the eight updates.
symbols.quote: For a segment of $\mathcal{W}$ with value $\xi$ and the corresponding segment of $\mathcal{T}$ with value $\eta$, the construction uses eight controlled updates.

symbols.name: Iverson bracket
symbols.meaning: The indicator that equals 1 when the statement P holds and 0 otherwise.
symbols.quote: Here $[P]$ is $1$ when $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise, and the updates run in order (1) to (8):

symbols.name: exceptional addresses
symbols.meaning: The set of addresses at which some guard used by the parallel stage lies outside its safe range.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the set of addresses at which some guard of the first $\nu-1$ segments of $\mathcal{W}$ or $\mathcal{T}$ lies outside this range.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each record, which the cost bounds divide by.
symbols.quote: Here $R$ is the number of bits in each record, and $\zeta=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ counts the bits of a stream position.

symbols.name: stream address length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits needed to write a position in the stream, ceiling of log base 2 of 2V.
symbols.quote: Here $R$ is the number of bits in each record, and $\zeta=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ counts the bits of a stream position.

relations.predicate: supplies the binary basis changes of
relations.quote: Packed selected-bit addition supplies the binary basis changes of the [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md).
Packed selected-bit addition contributes one term to the [cost table](cost-table.md) of the theorem.
Packed selected-bit addition acts on two disjoint [address fields](address-field.md) of equal width, the source $\mathcal{X}$ and the target $\mathcal{W}$.
Packed selected-bit addition uses its third chunk as [scratch storage](scratch-storage.md), $\mathcal{T}$, whose initial value is arbitrary and must be restored.
Packed selected-bit addition adds selected bits by [exclusive or](xor.md), so each selected bit of $\mathcal{W}$ is XORed with the selected bit of $\mathcal{X}$ in the same segment.

relations.predicate: updates its target chunk by controlled
relations.quote: Packed selected-bit addition updates its target chunk by controlled [cyclic shifts](cyclic-shift.md).
Packed selected-bit addition uses updates like the [Address shear](address-shear.md).
Packed selected-bit addition exchanges its chunks by the [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md) to bring a target chunk beside its controls.

relations.predicate: bounds its exceptional set by a
relations.quote: Packed selected-bit addition bounds its exceptional set by a [union bound](union-bound.md) over the $2(\nu-1)$ guards, so $\mathcal{B}$ holds at most a fraction $80(\nu-1)/2^{\mu}$ of all addresses.
Packed selected-bit addition is correct for every [payload](payload.md) it carries.
Packed selected-bit addition computes the [destination rank](destination-rank.md) of each extracted record, its position in the final order after the move.

relations.predicate: sorts the extracted records by a
relations.quote: Packed selected-bit addition sorts the extracted records by a [stable radix sort](stable-radix-sort.md) on these ranks, and reinserts each at its rank.
Packed selected-bit addition performs its basis changes in each [transform round](transform-round.md).
